judgments.description: One judgment per provision id listed in the document, in the order given.

clause_id.description: The provision id, copied exactly from the square brackets.

issues.description: Every construction issue this provision carries, one entry each, with its own probability. Only defects you can NAME go in the list. A provision with nothing to name for either type gets an empty list, and that is the ordinary answer -- most provisions get it. Otherwise normally exactly one entry. Two issues of one type, or issues of both types, are the exception -- give them only when the extra defect is obvious and carries a genuinely high probability of its own. A type with no entry is read as probability 0, which is what it means: nothing specific was found.

issue.description: Two sentences naming THIS specific defect: for risk type 1 the ambiguous term or the general-vs-specific tension; for risk type 2 the other provision it cannot be squared with, named. Never empty and never null -- an entry exists only because there is a defect to name. If you cannot name one, write no entry.

type.description: 1 for an intrinsic textual defect, visible in the provision itself. 2 for a defect in the provision's relationship to the rest of the instrument.

prob.description: Probability in (0, 1] that a court would have something to construe on account of THIS issue. Greater than zero: the entry exists because the defect does, and a defect you would put at 0 is one you should not have listed. Two decimal places, on a 0.01 grid (0.03, 0.17, 0.62) -- do not round to the nearest 0.05 or 0.1. The range is stated here and not as minimum/maximum, which structured output rejects on a number; the reader clamps it.
